title: Mutation Testing for Safety Property Coverage

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: mutation testing measures benchmark quality by introducing known defects and checking detection rates. Directly operationalizes meta-evaluation of safety benchmarks with every link explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning models to remove safety RLHF or fine-tune on harmful data, which demands advanced ML expertise and compute beyond Colab Pro. Not feasible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple mutation types across multiple benchmarks creates an open-ended project. No single clear first deliverable achievable in 30 hours for a beginner team.

novelty.reasoning: Mutation testing is well-established in software engineering but has not been formally applied to AI safety benchmarks. 'Safety Misalignment Against Large Language Models' (NDSS 2025) studies fine-tuning-based safety degradation but frames it as an attack, not as benchmark quality measurement. StrongREJECT provides a safety benchmark but no mutation-based meta-evaluation. The concept of deliberately introducing known safety defects (via RLHF removal, harmful fine-tuning) and measuring benchmark detection rates as a quality metric for safety benchmarks is a novel application of mutation testing principles to the AI safety evaluation domain. The main challenge is complexity, not lack of novelty.

existing_work: Safety Misalignment Against Large Language Models (NDSS 2025) - studies fine-tuning safety degradation as attack
StrongREJECT safety benchmark - benchmark that could be mutation-tested but no such analysis exists
Safe RLHF (ICLR 2024) - constrained safety optimization but not mutation testing
